thread:
Carla R: Heads up — large training cohort in eu-central-3 (~120 GPUs) started reporting 3-4x allreduce times and some jobs stuck at step 0 since ~06:40 UTC. Anyone changed networking or drivers this morning?

infra-bot: Deploybot: Automated rollout: OFED 5.12 + mlx5 FW 22.38 started in eu-central-3 at 06:15 UTC (batch 1/5).

Alice M: Yep we kicked that rollout at 06:15; batch 1 finished. I saw some WARNs from mlx5 on a few hosts during the rollout but thought they were transient.

Ben K: Seeing NCCL errors in a couple job logs: "NET/Plugin: failed to init ibv context" then later many "transport fallback to TCP" entries. If IB contexts fail we'll fall back and throughput tanks.

Dave O: Can you paste a short snippet of the nccl and kernel logs from one of impacted nodes? Also run `ibv_devinfo` and `ib_read_bw` if possible.

Carla R: Pasting minimal excerpts from job and host (sanitized):
```
# /var/log/nccl.log
[0] NCCL WARN NET/Plugin : failed to init ibv context (errno=22)
[0] NCCL INFO NET/Socket : using TCP fallback
[0] NCCL ERR Allreduce : timeout waiting for rank 2
```
```
# dmesg | tail
mlx5_core 0000:af:00.0: mlx5_core: MLX5: NIC FW 22.38 loaded
mlx5_core 0000:af:00.0: mlx5_core: Tx pacing: enabled
mlx5_core 0000:af:00.0: mlx5_core: CQ trim requested due to error
```
```
# ibv_devinfo
hca_id:mlx5_0
transport: InfiniBand (1)
phys_port_cnt: 2
link_layer: InfiniBand
```
```
# ib_read_bw -s 2
Post send failed: Invalid argument (22)
```

Ben K: "Invalid argument (22)" from ib verbs usually means the driver/firmware ABI mismatch or some missing ioctl support. Could be OFED/kernel combination. We pushed kernel 6.5.8 -> 6.6.0 on those hosts last night too.

Alice M: Ah — yes we rolled kernel 6.6.0 on the same subset at 02:30 UTC. So hosts with both kernel+fw/ofed updated are the ones impacted. Good call.

Dave O: Quick mitigation options: 1) Pause the OFED/fw rollout (stop further hosts), 2) Canary rollback mlx5 fw and OFED on a small set, 3) Force jobs to use TCP explicitly via NCCL env (NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1) so at least they make progress until we fix RDMA. Thoughts?

Carla R: Option 3 will make progress but 3-4x slowdown vs RDMA. Given SPO, I'd rather jobs make progress than be stuck. We can set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 at scheduler level for the affected queue as temporary.

Ben K: I'd rather validate ibv stack first — `modinfo mlx5_core`, `grep mlx5 /var/log/kern.log`, and `mlxconfig -d /dev/mst/mt4215 query` if drivers expose it. Also check if kernel's xps/txqueue params changed.

Alice M: I'll pause the rollout right now (ACTION). Rolling back batch 1 on 6 hosts as canary. If rollback fixes ibv_read_bw that confirms compatibility issue.

infra-bot: Action logged: "rollout paused" by Alice M at 07:05 UTC. Patchset hold applied to euc3.

Dave O: Cost/ops note — ~120 GPUs idled or slowed for ~2 hours. If we force TCP we'll get throughput but increased job runtime and cluster cost. Rough estimate: extra 30% GPU-hours for the cohort if TCP-only.

Carla R: Please toggle NCCL env on the training queue in the next 10m if rollback will take >15m. I'll inform the ML teams.

Ben K: After we have a canary rollback result run these checks on both good and bad hosts and paste outputs: `ibv_devinfo`, `ib_read_bw -s 2`, `ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "rx|tx|err"`, `dmesg | tail -n 200 | grep mlx5`. Also capture `lsmod | grep mlx` and `modinfo mlx5_core`.

Alice M: Canaries rolled back at 07:25 UTC — preliminary: ib_read_bw now shows expected numbers (~95 Gbps), no more errno 22. Keeping rollback on those 6 hosts for 30m observation window.

Carla R: Confirming jobs on the canary hosts resumed and allreduce times returned to baseline. I'm pushing NCCL env change to queue still until we finish validation.

Dave O: Next steps:
- Pause further fw/ofed/kernel rollout in euc3 (done).
- Run full delta analysis between canary (rolled back) and impacted hosts (good/bad diffs).
- Reproduce in lab with same kernel/OFED/fw combos.
- Coordinate vendor ticket with Broadcom/Mellanox; include `ibv_devinfo`, MLX logs, and ib_read_bw traces.

Ben K: Also note: there were a couple of hosts showing "Tx pacing: enabled" in dmesg after fw update. That pacing mode combined with a kernel change could break verb params. We'll include that signal in the vendor report.

Alice M: I'll open an internal incident and vendor ticket now, include canary artifacts and set priority P1 for eu-central-3 degraded. Assigning to @Ben K for logs and @Dave O for rollback orchestration.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0456 (eu-central-3 RDMA regress). Ticket to vendor opened: Mellanox case 54321.

Carla R: Thanks — I'll update ML teams and set scheduled window for a full rollback if vendor doesn't have quick fix.

Dave O: If vendor fix will take >24h we'll plan to pin kernel+OFED/fw to last-good on all nodes and re-schedule rollout after testing.

Alice M: Good work — updates in this thread as we get vendor feedback.
